exercises.title: Embedded C, Arduino, and PlatformIO: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: A variable is written in an ISR and read in the main loop. What does correct firmware need?
choices: Declare it const so the compiler can cache it
Declare it volatile and read it atomically, briefly disabling interrupts when it spans several bytes
Nothing special, since the compiler always re-reads globals
Declare it volatile, because volatile alone makes every access atomic
hints: volatile prevents caching; it does not make multi-byte access atomic.

exercises.title: Embedded C, Arduino, and PlatformIO: worked analysis
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Refactor blocking sensor-and-button code into a timed state machine with testable pure functions.

Show assumptions, equations, units, standard-value choices, ratings, tolerance effects, and the measurements that would verify the result.
checklist: I drew or described the complete source and return path.
I carried units and checked the order of magnitude.
I checked ratings and at least one worst-case condition.
I wrote an observable verification step before viewing the solution.
hints: Start with a symbolic relationship before substituting numbers.
Separate typical behavior from guaranteed limits and add measurement tolerance.
exercises.solutionMarkdown:
## Reference solution

Replace delay-driven sequencing with a state enum, event inputs, and elapsed-time comparisons using wrap-safe unsigned subtraction. Keep hardware access behind small driver interfaces and pure decision logic in ordinary functions. Mark memory volatile only when it can change outside normal flow; volatile does not make compound operations atomic.

The governing principle is: **write explicit hardware boundaries and deterministic state machines instead of delay-driven sketches**. Define every reference direction and convert values to coherent SI units. Compare the result with component ratings and standard available values, then report a bounded expectation that includes tolerance, temperature, supply variation, and instrument loading.

### Verification evidence

1. Power off and confirm wiring, polarity, and discharge state.
2. Configure a conservative current limit.
3. Predict source current and the critical node voltages or waveform features.
4. Power on and compare the first measurement with the bounded prediction.
5. Stop if current, temperature, smell, or waveform exceeds the safe bound.

The notebook should make both the reasoning and bench test independently reproducible.

exercises.title: Embedded C, Arduino, and PlatformIO: measurement and fault investigation
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Plan or perform a low-voltage investigation of **volatile used as synchronization, signed overflow, blocking delay, magic register constants**. Record a safe setup, predicted healthy evidence, observed evidence, one hypothesis at a time, and the final verification.
checklist: I documented the de-energized inspection and safe current limit.
I recorded expected healthy readings before measuring.
I used one falsifiable hypothesis at a time.
I included final evidence that distinguishes cause from symptom.
hints: Measure the supply current and block boundaries before probing internal details.
Change only one condition between measurements.
